answer: Sybil resistance can come from retroactive audit rather than entry cost. Each attestation lands in a copper ledger of immutable receipts, and a long horizon of closed epochs stays open to surprise replay: a beacon later picks one epoch and re-runs it against a mirrored peer set that never saw the original votes. Honest agents reproduce their verdicts; puppets copying a shared answer drift, and every receipt from that epoch is clawed back. Audits reach far behind the signing moment, so a farmer must keep each identity coherent for months, paying continuous inference instead of one deposit.
